title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (Analysis situs, 3rd version, 1986): Grothendieck works with 'figures' built from a set M of basic cells (here 'simplexes'). Figures carry three relations: ≤ (sub-figure), ≪ (a significance or 'tight' inclusion relation) and ≍ (compatibility, meaning the pieces meet in a common sub-figure). There is a realization map φ from these abstract figures to ordinary figures, or 'ombrées' (shadowed sets), in a set or space. omb(F) = |φ(F)| is the underlying point set, the 'shadow'. The proposition under proof says φ reflects the relations: (a) a statement about sub-figures, (b) φ(F) ≪ φ(G) ⇒ F ≪ G, (c) φ(F) ≍ φ(G) ⇒ F ≍ G. It is proved under conditions (i) and (ii) on the structure.

On p.56 he is proving (c) without assuming φ injective. He reaches a hypothetical bad configuration: X ∈ L'∖L and Y ∈ L''∖L with X ≠ Y and φ(X) = φ(Y), whose largest common sub-figure is X∩L = Y∩L.

Page 57 does three things.

(1) It records two remarks about such a configuration. Necessarily omb(X) = omb(Y), both equal to |φ(X)| = |φ(Y)|. Also L = ∅ cannot a priori be excluded.

(2) It shows the configuration really occurs.
- Take a topological space X and let M be the 'simplexes' in X: subsets with a simplicial (affine) structure transported by a homeomorphism.
- Use the usual face relation for ≤, respecting the affine structures.
- For ≪, and likewise ≍, require that |σ|∩|σ'| be empty or a common sub-simplex.
- This yields a structure of figures satisfying all conditions except (ii).
- Now put two different affine structures on one arc A ⊂ X homeomorphic to [0,1]. This gives 1-simplices X ≠ Y with L = ∂X = ∂Y (the two endpoints) and φ(X) = φ(Y).
- Hence φ(X) ≍ φ(Y) and φ(X) ≪ φ(Y), but neither X ≍ Y nor X ≪ Y. So (b) and (c) fail, φ is not injective, and (ii) fails.

(3) It extracts a corollary. Condition (i) implies (ii) together with injectivity of φ, and conversely ('plus précisément (i) ⇒ (ii) + φ injectif ⇒ (i)'). An earlier hoped-for version, that injectivity of φ on M alone suffices, is struck out as 'pas vrai'. He notes that (ii) plus injectivity of φ|M should give (b) and (c), with (a) already proved. He then resumes the proof of (c) using injectivity of φ, so that φ(H) is the largest common sub-figure of φ(F), φ(G) (continued p.58, where (b) is found to be false via polyhedral vs set-theoretic ≪).
errors: The Cor is stated hesitantly; the final reading is the equivalence (i) ⇔ (ii) + φ injective. The page does not prove the converse direction; it is only asserted.

The example is sketched informally. The 'affine structure on an arc' is meant as a transported simplex structure (homeomorphism to Δ1 up to affine change). Distinctness of X and Y as elements of M while φ(X) = φ(Y) is the whole point; it is correct, though M is not precisely defined on the page.

The struck-out claim that injectivity of φ|M alone suffices is correctly retracted. The hoped-for implication (ii) + φ|M injective ⇒ (b) turns out false on the next page, so the plan stated here is partly wrong.

ideas.what: Abstract 'figures' with relations ≤, ≪, ≍ and a realization map φ to point-set shadows (omb); the question when φ reflects these relations.
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatics of tame/polyhedral topology; realization of abstract complexes (cf. face posets, regular CW complexes, o-minimal cell structures)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck's programme of 'topologie modérée' (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984); formal o-minimal theory by van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight
ideas.where_published: Only the programmatic idea in Esquisse d'un programme §5; this axiomatics remains in the unpublished Analysis situs notes

ideas.what: Counterexample: two distinct simplicial/affine structures on the same topological arc give distinct cells with the same shadow and boundary, so realization is not injective and relations are not reflected.
ideas.modern_name: Non-uniqueness of PL/affine structures on a topological cell; 'tame' structure must be data, not property

ideas.what: Corollary: condition (i) ⇔ condition (ii) + injectivity of φ.
ideas.modern_name: Technical lemma internal to the axiom system

deep.surprise_reason: Routine working-out within an unpublished axiomatic attempt at tame topology. The counterexample (two PL structures on an arc) is elementary, and the corollary is an internal technical equivalence. Interesting only as documentation of how Grothendieck tested his axioms for 'figures'.
transcription_corrections: '(mais en remplaçant les structures affines)' should probably read '(mais en respectant les structures affines)'.
'M ⋠ itou (...)' is likely '≍ itou (en sous-simplexes communs)': compatibility ≍ defined likewise, i.e. intersection empty or a common sub-simplex.
'Donc ici φ(X) ≰ φ(Y) et φ(X) ≪ φ(Y), X ≰ Y ni X ≪ Y' should read 'mais ici φ(X) ≍ φ(Y) et φ(X) ≪ φ(Y), mais X ≭ Y ni X ≪ Y'. The symbol is the compatibility relation ≍, not ≤.
Marginal note: 'plus précisément (i) ⇒ (ii)+φ injectif ⇒ (i)', with an arrow inserting it after 'Cor'.
'(ii) + φ|M inj. ⇒ b, c reste à prouver (a a été prouvé déjà)'.
